archetype.name: Game Manager (accuracy-first backup)
archetype.definition: A short-area, rhythm passer who completes a high share of quick, safe throws and avoids turnovers, but rarely pushes the ball past the sticks and takes too many sacks when the first read isn't there.

report.headline: A tidy, low-risk relief run ended by a torn throwing elbow
report.take:
Minshew's 2026 is over. He tore the UCL in his right throwing elbow, landed on Injured Reserve, and faces season-ending surgery with an estimated return date of 2027-02-15. He now sits fourth on Arizona's depth chart. What's left to assess is what his brief run says about him, and it says what his career has always said: a competent, accurate backup who keeps the offense on schedule and doesn't lose games with the football, without the downfield aggression to lift a struggling offense.

The season line flatters him because it is really two very different games. In relief at Dallas, against the defense now ranked last in EPA, he went 17/23 for 188 yards, 3 touchdowns and +13.4 EPA on only 42% of the snaps. In the start at Seattle, against the fifth-ranked defense, the same approach produced -5.8 EPA, no touchdowns, 3 sacks and a 10.3% bad-throw rate in a 3-17 loss. His line as a starter (-0.174 EPA per dropback, 5.53 yards per attempt) is the more honest read on what Arizona was getting week to week. The 10.15 CPOE, 2nd of 54, is real accuracy on easy throws. It is not a sign of a breakout.

The style shows clearly in the tracking data. He threw aggressively into tight windows only 7.55% of the time, his intended air yards sat at 6.98, and his average throw landed 1.45 yards short of the sticks. That approach keeps interceptions at zero, and he had none on 53 attempts. It also caps third downs, where he converted just 35.7%. The red-zone touchdowns and the gaudy 1.353 EPA on intermediate throws come from a handful of attempts (7 intermediate, 13 red zone), much of it at Dallas, so read them as hints, not traits.

The flaw that does carry across years is the sacks. He was pressured on only 15.8% of dropbacks, 6th-lowest of 42, yet turned 44.4% of that pressure into sacks, 41st of 42. His career pressure-to-sack ranks have sat in the back half nearly every season (46th of 59 in 2020, 40th of 66 in 2023, 42nd of 60 in 2024). He holds the ball looking for the safe completion rather than throwing it away or creating outside the pocket: zero scrambles this year. That is who he is, and it is a big part of why he has been a bridge starter rather than a long-term answer.

strengths.title: Accurate on the throws he takes
strengths.body: He completed 71.7% of his passes with a CPOE of 10.15, 2nd at the position, and 84.6% on throws under 10 air yards. That comes from a quick, defined-read approach (2.5-second time to throw) more than from difficult throws. His career CPOE has swung from strong (2020, 2021) to poor (2019, 2023), so the level here is partly sample, but clean short-area accuracy is a fair baseline for him.

strengths.title: Ball security, no giveaways
strengths.body: He had no interceptions and no lost fumbles, and his 7.5% bad-throw rate ranked 1st of 42. The conservative target selection produces this: few tight-window throws means few chances for defenders. Over his career he has had multi-interception seasons, so a clean slate on 53 attempts partly reflects volume. Still, a low-risk distributor is the profile.

strengths.title: Found Wilson and McBride
strengths.body: His production ran through two targets. Michael Wilson added 8.7 EPA on 14 targets and Trey McBride 5.3 EPA on 14. Throws to the left and middle (0.614 and 0.52 EPA per play) were far more productive than his heavy rightward volume. These are small samples, but they show he was reading the field toward Arizona's best options.

concerns.title: Season-ending elbow surgery
concerns.body: A torn UCL in the throwing elbow, with surgery and a projected return of 2027-02-15, ends his year outright. For a 30-year-old backup whose value rests on accuracy and quick processing, a throwing-arm repair also clouds his market next season until he shows he is healthy.

concerns.title: Sacks when the first read closes
concerns.body: He was rarely pressured but converted pressure into sacks at a 44.4% rate, 41st of 42. His career shows the same pattern, a long-standing trait rather than a blip. With no scrambles to offset it, the sacks are pure cost, and they hit hardest against a blitz-happy Seattle that sent extra rushers 11 times.

concerns.title: Short of the sticks, stalls on third
concerns.body: His average throw landed 1.45 yards short of the first-down marker, and his aggressiveness was just 7.55%. The result was a 35.7% third-down conversion rate and -0.178 EPA per play on third down. Against a good defense that can rally and tackle short throws, as Seattle did, this ceiling shows up quickly.

trend.note: His season peaked in the Dallas relief outing (+13.4 EPA against the league's worst defense), dropped hard in the Seattle start (-5.8 EPA against a top-five unit), and then ended with the elbow injury.

nextGame.headline: He won't play; Arizona's next QB faces a stiff test
nextGame.body:
Minshew is on Injured Reserve after elbow surgery and will not face Kansas City. The matchup is still worth noting for what it would have asked of his style. The Chiefs' defense ranks 6th in EPA and 4th against short throws (-0.136 EPA). That is exactly where a short-area, sticks-averse passer lives, and their 2nd and 5th ranks in EPA allowed to WR1 and WR2 would squeeze Arizona's top targets. The Book has the Cardinals as 16.5-point road underdogs with a 41.5 total, which points to a trailing, pass-heavy script for whoever starts.

Availability on Arizona's side makes it harder for the replacement. Center Hjalte Froholdt (100% of snaps) is out with a concussion, and guard Jon Gaines and tackle Jayden Williams are also out, leaving a patched-up interior. The one relief is that Kansas City's pass rush has been modest (27th in sack rate and hit rate), and defensive tackle Peter Woods is out. On the Chiefs' offense, Kenneth Walker III is out, but their 6th-ranked offense still sets up a game Arizona will likely be chasing.

keyMatchups.title: Short-throw defense versus a dink offense
keyMatchups.body: Kansas City allows -0.136 EPA on short throws, 4th in the league, which would take away the area where Minshew created most of his volume. Whoever replaces him inherits the same problem if Arizona keeps the ball under 10 yards.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted Arizona interior line
keyMatchups.body: With the starting center and two other linemen out, protection and snap-to-snap communication suffer. Kansas City's weak pass-rush numbers soften that somewhat.

keyMatchups.title: Two-plus-score underdog script
keyMatchups.body: A 16.5-point spread means likely catch-up mode, which inflates attempts but invites turnovers and sacks for a backup QB.

nextGame.watch: Who Arizona turns to at QB behind a line missing its center, and whether it keeps Minshew's short, quick-game structure or tries to push the ball downfield against Kansas City.

restOfSeason.body:
There is no rest of season for Minshew: season-ending surgery on his throwing elbow rules him out, and his projections are zero across the board. His 2026 goes down as a small, split sample: one excellent relief appearance against a bottom defense and one flat start against a good one. The steadier signals line up with his career profile, which are the quick, accurate short game, minimal turnovers, and a stubbornly high pressure-to-sack rate. The flashy pieces, like the intermediate and red-zone efficiency, were too thin to call real.

Looking ahead, the question is the elbow. A UCL repair on a 30-year-old journeyman's throwing arm, with a projected return in February, makes his 2027 role as a bridge or backup depend on how he throws in the spring. When healthy, expect the same player: a safe, on-schedule passer who keeps an offense functional for a few weeks but doesn't raise its ceiling.
swingFactors: UCL surgery recovery and offseason throwing

confidence.note: Season-ending surgery settles his outlook; the performance read rests on only two games.
